tob-10483: Written for the general reader, Israel Abrahams’s ‘Judaism’ explains the faith as Jews themselves lived it — the Sabbath table, the synagogue, the daily prayers, the festivals through the year. He stresses practice over doctrine and home over temple. First published around 1907, it remains a clear, humane doorway into a religion often misunderstood from the outside.
tob-13783: Helena Blavatsky turns storyteller in this collection of eerie tales — haunted houses, astral doubles, and encounters with the uncanny drawn from her occult worldview. Written to thrill as well as to teach, the stories hint at the hidden forces she believed govern our lives. They show the founder of Theosophy as a writer of gothic imagination.
tob-4083: This set gathers the early verse of William Butler Yeats — the dreamy, twilight poems that made his name. Here are ‘The Lake Isle of Innisfree’ and the love poems to Maud Gonne, steeped in Irish old lore. The book shows the young Yeats before statecraft and age deepened his note.
tob-13583: The whole King James Bible — all sixty-six books, from Genesis to Revelation, in the 1611 English that shaped the tongue itself. Its rhythms run through books, laws, and common talk. Four hundred years it has been the English world’s Bible.
tob-4283: E. A. Wallis Budge’s Dead-Book — the Ani papyrus — gives old Egypt’s great burial writ, the soul-fare spells. The Medici printing sets picture-signs beside Englishing. Budge’s toil first showed Egypt’s afterworld to common folk everywhere. A landmark of Egypt-lore.
tob-9283: Peterson’s Catholic wordbook piece treats the Apostle-Fathers — the first Christian writers past the apostles, Clement, Ignatius, and Polycarp. His short reckoning is a clear door to the under-apostle age. The piece serves as a handy gate to earliest Christianity.
tob-14183: R. H. Charles’s Cast-Out Writ, book one, is the great English garland of the Old Testament’s barred books, from Tobit to the Maccabees. His Englishings with learned fore-words set the scholar’s mark. The work stays the needful handbook for the field.
tob-14483: Wilhelm Reich’s Headlong Man is the soul-leech’s study of the driven kind — blind headlongness, soul-armor, and the missing helm. His early clinic-work fore-ran his later mooted thinkings. It shows Reich ere the orgone years, a gifted healer. The book is weighty for soul-leech story.
cia-0000105883: From September 1964, a report on a pro-communist Indonesian army officer who believed war with Britain was unavoidable and that Indonesia should prepare for it. Britain was backing the new federation of Malaysia, which Jakarta opposed in its Confrontation campaign. The document reveals how far some officers were willing to push the conflict.
cia-0000107983: An untitled March 1978 document on Pakistan's strong motivation to develop its nuclear capability. After India's 1974 nuclear test, Islamabad was determined not to be left behind — whatever the cost. The report captures the CIA recognizing, early and clearly, the drive that would make Pakistan a nuclear power.
cia-0000108483: A weekly terrorism situation report dated August 5, 1981 — the archive's spelling says Aigist, a small human error in a serious file. By 1981 the weekly rhythm of global terrorism reporting was well established. The document is routine, and that is the point: vigilance had become a habit.
cia-0000119583: A November 1964 intelligence memorandum on Czechoslovakia's new policy within the Soviet bloc. Step by step, Prague was asserting itself — and Moscow was taking notes. The document traces the slow-motion collision between reform and empire.
cia-0000126983: A November 1974 report on Zambian President Kaunda's visit reflecting Soviet interest in the region. Moscow was courting frontline African states as the Angola crisis brewed. The document shows superpower courtship: a presidential visit, read as a move on the chessboard.
cia-0000132283: Situation Report 592 on West European reactions to Saddam's speech. The Iraqi leader's words were parsed in every European chancellery. The document gathers the continent's verdict: defiance heard, resolve unshaken.
cia-0000132483: Item 6 in the April 1960 series: Brazil restricting the Cuban president's tour. Brasilia was cooling toward Havana — the continent's giant, keeping its distance. The document is the cold shoulder, documented: the welcome, withdrawn.
cia-0000132683: A 1961 report: the USSR issuing a statement on Cuba. Moscow's words were policy — the patron, speaking. The document is the statement: the superpower, declaring.
cia-0000136183: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting information on rumors of increased fighter or bomber strength — the truncated title cuts off whose. The enemy's air power, rumored. The document is the rumor: the aircraft, counted — or imagined.
cia-0000136283: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN with a reply to a deleted recipient — suggestions on announcing a provisional something, the truncated title cuts off the noun. The announcement, advised. The entry is the reply: the suggestions, offered — the recipient, hidden.
cia-0000136983: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN — the archive's spelling says senor — recommending a statement be made by Calligeris, the truncated title suggests. The proclamation, urged. The entry is the recommendation: the statement, proposed.
cia-0000138983: A 1946 military information report on Russian aid to Chinese communists in Manchuria. Moscow was arming Mao's forces as the Chinese civil war reignited. The document is the aid: the weapons, flowing — the alliance, forming.
un-ga-res-1883: General Assembly Resolution 1883, adopted in 1963. The early 1960s Assembly wrestled with decolonization, disarmament, and development. The catalog holds the number and year; the resolution's operative paragraphs hold its purpose.
un-ga-res-a-69-83: Resolution A/69/83, adopted in 2015 — the session's spillover year. The designation and year are preserved; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-183: Security Council Resolution 183, adopted in 1964. The Council deciding. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1383: Security Council Resolution 1383, adopted in 2001 — aligned. The Afghanistan year's Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1483: Security Council Resolution 1483, adopted in May 2003 — the post-invasion Iraq resolution, recognizing the US and UK as occupying powers and lifting the sanctions on Iraq. The Council ratified the new order in Baghdad. The resolution is the recognition: the occupation, legitimized — the sanctions, ended.
un-sc-res-1783: Security Council Resolution 1783, cataloged with the year 2008 — the numbering suggests 2007, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1883: Security Council Resolution 1883, adopted in 2009 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
cia-0000132783: A 1960 CIA file on Cuba and the Caribbean, numbered 0000132783 — the Cuba run continues into the new shard. The island and its neighbors, one more folder. The document is the continuation: the watch, unbroken.
cia-0000136683: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136683. The Spanish-language record of the defeated invasion. The entry is the defeat's record: the invasion, lost — the papers, kept.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d83: The Secretary of State to the Acting Secretary of State Stettinius — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 83. The secretary wrote his stand-in. The memo is the handoff: the office, covered.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d183: The Secretary of State to the President, November 2, 1943 — Document 183. The next day, another. The memo is the cadence: the briefings, daily.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d283: A memorandum by Lieutenant General Stilwell's political adviser, Davies — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 283. The adviser's paper. The memo is the adviser's: Davies, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d383: The Secretary of State to the President, November 27, 1943 — Document 383. The department briefed the White House. The memo is the briefing: the secretary, informing.
arxiv-2605-09083: Societies get stuck: everyone knows the equilibrium is bad, yet nobody moves first. Madjid Eshaghi Gordji, Esmaiel Abounoori, and Mohamadali Berahma study status-quo inertia, how institutional design can break it, and what equilibrium transitions look like. The 2026 paper is game theory for reformers.
arxiv-2605-09183: Imitation learning copies experts — but under shifted dynamics, some demonstrations mislead. Surbhi Goel, Jonathan Pei, and James Wang learn when to stop: selective imitation that skips the bad demos. The 2026 paper is about knowing which expert examples not to follow.
arxiv-2605-09283: AI generates oceans of content, but reusing it reliably — knowing which prompt made what — is unsolved. Shusaku Egami and Masahiro Hamasaki propose a prompt-aware structuring framework for the agentic era. The 2026 paper organizes AI output by its origins for reliable reuse.
arxiv-2605-09483: Why do some people fall for misinformation while others shrug it off? This 2026 paper builds a cognitively grounded Bayesian framework for susceptibility — modeling belief updates the way minds actually work. It is computational social science on the mechanics of being fooled.
arxiv-2605-09583: The comaximal graph of a Lie algebra connects subalgebras that together span everything — a social network of subalgebras. David A. Towers, Yesneri Zuleta, and Ismael Gutierrez study its structure for finite-dimensional Lie algebras. The 2026 paper is algebraic graph theory with a Lie-theoretic flavor.
arxiv-2605-09683: Rook theory counts placements on chessboards; normal ordering tames unruly operator products; the q-deformed Ore algebra generalizes the whole algebraic setting. Matthias Schork weaves all three threads together, including the polynomial generalization. The 2026 paper is elegant combinatorics meets quantum algebra.
arxiv-2605-09883: Vision reasoning in Cartesian coordinates may take a shortcut — missing what polar coordinates reveal. Xia Hu, Zhenrui Yue, Brian Potetz, and colleagues re-evaluate vision reasoning in polar coordinate space. The 2026 paper is computer vision with a change of coordinates.
plos-pone-0003383: Plant geneticists untangled a metabolic traffic jam in this 2008 study of the GABA shunt, a pathway that reroutes steps of the cell's energy cycle in both plants and microbes. When one enzyme, succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase, is broken, plants suffer badly. Mutations in a second enzyme, GABA transaminase (POP2), suppressed that damage, revealing how the pathway balances itself.
plos-pone-0003483: Cardiologists parsed diabetes' danger after heart attacks in this 2008 study. Diabetes worsens the outlook after acute coronary syndrome, but the team found the added risk depends on whether it was a first event or a recurrence and on the patient's overall profile. The nuanced results help doctors tailor follow-up care for diabetic heart patients.
plos-pone-0003583: Geneticists built a heart-focused gene chip in this 2008 paper. The cardiovascular gene-centric array packed 50,000 DNA variants chosen for their relevance to heart disease, a purpose-built tool for large association studies. The design and implementation details give the community a shared platform for hunting cardiac risk genes.
plos-pone-0003683: In 2008, Kamath, Rochat, and Valenti found newborn shots can work like adult ones. A new adjuvant let neonatal vaccines trigger grown-up style T-cell and dendritic-cell responses against mycobacteria. The adult-like response in newborns is a step toward TB vaccines that protect from the very start of life.
plos-pone-0003783: Kantor, Pinchasi, and Mintz found a single mutation keeping brain cells in permanent alarm in this 2008 paper. A change in translation initiation factor 2B left oligodendrocytes, the brain's myelin makers, stuck in a hyper stress state. The result explains the white-matter loss of Vanishing White Matter disease.
plos-pone-0003883: A 2008 health-economics study priced rehab for clogged leg arteries. New cardiac and vascular rehab strategies for coronary artery disease patients were weighed for cost against benefit. The analysis guides hospitals toward rehab programs that deliver the most heart health per dollar.
plos-pone-0003983: In 2008, Ikegaya, Matsumoto, and Chiou asked if neurons replay exact patterns. They tested whether precisely repeated intracellular synaptic patterns could arise by chance. The statistics showed millisecond-precise repeats beating the long odds against chance. The finding suggests neural circuits can be far more exact than assumed.
plos-pone-0004083: In 2008, Hashiguchi, Furuta, and Nishida sniffed out fish evolution. Teleost fishes lack a vomeronasal organ, so smell receptors crowd the main olfactory sheet. Odorant and pheromone receptor gene families evolved under shifting pressures. The fish nose tells a leaner story than the mammal's.
plos-pone-0004183: In 2009, Qin, Ho, and Wang found a new Alzheimer's clue in a skin protein. S100A7, with non-amyloidogenic alpha-secretase activity, marked Alzheimer's disease clearly. The protein pushed amyloid processing down a safer path. The new biomarker could aid early detection efforts.
plos-pone-0004283: In 2009, De Lisle, Meldi, and Roach linked gut trouble to mast cells. Cystic fibrosis mice showed mast-cell-driven gastrointestinal dysmotility. The gut's poor movement traced to immune overactivity. The finding suggests mast-cell-targeted relief. Calming mast cells could ease CF gut symptoms.
plos-pone-0358883: Chronic hives — itchy welts that appear without a clear trigger — may signal trouble beyond the skin. This study finds that people with moderate-to-severe chronic spontaneous urticaria face a higher risk of immune-mediated diseases, where the immune system turns on the body itself. The link suggests doctors treating stubborn hives should also watch for related immune conditions.
plos-pone-0357783: Oil drilling mud is chemistry’s dirty secret — but greener additives exist. This study tested pistachio shell powder, magnesium oxide, and carbon black as green additives in water-based drilling mud. The performance results show which waste-derived ingredients can replace harsher chemicals without losing function.
plos-pone-0355783: Shoppers say they’ll choose green packaging — then don’t. This ERP brain-wave study probed the intention-behavior gap in decisions about green express packaging. The neural signals reveal where good intentions die, giving eco-packaging designers clues about what actually moves a hand at checkout.
plos-pone-0356883: Bad prescribing mixes drugs that should never meet. This systematic review examined deterministic and stochastic interventions to reduce drug–drug interactions in inappropriate prescribing. The evidence synthesis shows which strategies actually clean up dangerous combinations in real-world practice.
plos-pone-0356783: Telling people their values matter may make health messages land better. This study tested incorporating public values into public health communications — value affirmations — on vaccination intentions and trust in the US. The effects show whether affirming someone’s identity opens their mind to vaccines.
plos-pone-0355683: Having kids changes academic careers — differently for mothers and fathers. This paper studied parenthood and care in academia through publication counts, self-assessed productivity, and gendered differences. The numbers document the parenthood penalty in hard data and show exactly where it falls hardest.
plos-pone-0358183: Kids with flexible flat feet often walk normally — but something compensates upstream. This dual-level study analyzed static alignment and dynamic movement, finding compensatory proximal malalignment despite preserved overall gait. The hidden misalignments matter for hips and knees over a lifetime of walking.
plos-pone-0352583: Rural Chinese clinics need help managing sick children where doctors are scarce. This cluster randomized controlled trial assessed an electronic platform for managing childhood illnesses — testing both accuracy and efficiency. The trial results show whether the digital tool genuinely improves care in the villages that need it most.
plos-pone-0356383: Rice diseases threaten harvests — and farmers need instant, on-the-spot diagnosis. IoT-RiceMobileNet is an improved lightweight MobileNetV2 model for real-time multi-class rice disease detection using IoT devices. The phone-ready model effectively brings the plant doctor directly to the paddy field.
plos-pone-0357983: Seeing the speaker’s mouth boosts hearing in noise — even for cochlear implant users. This study measured the impact of visual mouth image presentation on speech perception in noise, in both normal-hearing subjects and implant users. The measured visual boost quantifies lip-reading’s genuine power.
plos-pone-0357383: Melanoma in Xinjiang, China, presents its own distinct clinical profile. This retrospective cohort study examined the clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis of melanoma in the region. The regional data give local oncologists the evidence they need to tailor care to their population.
plos-pone-0356183: What students ask AI chatbots reveals how deeply they’re thinking. This paper studied static and longitudinal questioning patterns in student–LLM dialogue alongside self-reported cognitive engagement. The patterns show when AI genuinely aids learning — and when it merely shortcuts the hard thinking.
plos-pone-0357483: Common-cold coronaviruses never stop evolving. This paper tracked the spatiotemporal dynamics and phylogeography of HCoV-NL63 and HCoV-OC43 across Thailand in 2024–2025. The genomic surveillance maps where these familiar viruses are moving — and how they’re changing as they go.
plos-pone-0351883: Sulfate-contaminated soils must be solidified so their salts can’t migrate. This paper built a water and salt migration model for solidified sulfate-contaminated soil made with full solid-waste cementitious materials. The model predicts whether the containment will hold over time.
plos-pone-0356683: America’s blood supply depends on knowing exactly which blood types are out there. This paper mapped ABO and RhD blood group antigen frequencies in patients and blood donors, with implications for the U.S. blood supply. The frequency data help blood banks stock what the population actually needs.
plos-pone-0353983: Forecasting COVID-19’s next moves by state required better data than raw case counts. This paper forecasted cases across US states using reconstructed incidence data — correcting for testing gaps and delays. The reconstructed-data approach produced forecasts that tracked reality more faithfully.
plos-pone-0353483: Malaria’s geography in Bangladesh is shifting — and Bayesian maps can track it. This paper applied Bayesian disease mapping models to the spatial analysis of malaria. The probabilistic maps give health officials a sharper picture of where the parasite persists and where elimination is within reach.
plos-pone-0351683: Water invading marker beds can doom a wellbore’s casing — a catastrophic and costly failure. This paper studied the evolution and prevention of such casing failure induced by marker bed water invasion. The engineering analysis points to prevention strategies that keep wells intact and productive.
plos-pone-0355383: Does the light children live under shape their myopia? This paper published a protocol for a systematic review of spectral characteristics of light and their association with myopia progression in children. The planned synthesis could reveal whether tweaking classroom and home lighting slows the myopia epidemic.
plos-pone-0356283: How do we judge a smile that follows an angry face? This paper studied gaze allocation and evaluations of dynamic smiles after angry versus neutral expressions. The findings reveal how emotional context rewires our reading of facial expressions moment by moment.
plos-pone-0356483: Building a comfortable prosthetic socket is part science, part art — and AI can help. This paper developed and applied a prosthetist-specific rectification template based on artificial intelligence for fabricating transfemoral prosthetic sockets. The AI template encodes expert judgment, bringing master-prosthetist quality to more amputees.
plos-pone-0355483: Hypertensive Ethiopians’ kidneys decline at rates that were poorly documented. This five-year retrospective follow-up study measured chronic kidney disease progression and its predictors in hypertensive patients. The findings give Ethiopian clinicians the risk factors that flag whose kidneys are failing fastest.
plos-pone-0354883: Creatine supplements during dialysis — could they fight the muscle wasting of kidney failure? This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled pilot studied the feasibility, safety, and tolerability of intradialytic creatine. The findings test whether a simple supplement can help dialysis patients keep their strength.
europmc-pmc2801183: Heat waves kill, but not everyone equally. This 2009 paper maps which communities are most vulnerable to extreme heat. The authors combine health, social, and environmental data to pinpoint the neighborhood factors that raise heat risk. The maps give cities a practical guide for aiming cooling centers, outreach, and emergency plans where they are needed most.
europmc-pmc2826283: Inhaled nanoparticles go somewhere in the body, and this 2010 paper tracks their journey. The authors review how these tiny particles deposit in the lungs and move through the body over time. Their synthesis covers deposition and biokinetics together. The work is essential background for judging nanoparticle safety.
europmc-pmc2843083: Cancer registries report trends as average annual percent change, but the calculation has subtleties. This 2009 paper explains how to estimate that figure properly in trend analysis. The authors clarify the method behind a ubiquitous statistic. Their guidance keeps epidemiologists' trend claims honest.
europmc-pmc2848183: Judging the quality of measurement studies requires a good checklist. This 2010 paper clarifies the COSMIN checklist for evaluating the methodological quality of studies on measurement properties. The authors explain what each item means. Their clarification made the tool usable for reviewers of health questionnaires and tests.
europmc-pmc2885083: Algal toxins poison water worldwide, and this 2010 review tackles four bad ones. The authors cover how microcystin, nodularin, saxitoxin, and cylindrospermopsin are built, how they harm, and the genes behind them. Their roundup aids finding and fighting these poisons. The review is a go-to guide for keeping water safe.
europmc-pmc2952083: Antioxidant pills are not pure good. This 2010 review argues exogenous antioxidants are double-edged swords: helpful at physiologic doses, harmful at high ones. The authors weigh both edges of the evidence. Their overview tempers supplement hype with caution. Megadose users should read it first.
europmc-pmc2978683: Coastal plants handle salt differently, and this 2010 paper finds the gene. The authors show a coastal cline in sodium accumulation in Arabidopsis is driven by natural variation in the AtHKT1;1 transporter. Their work links gene to environment. The finding aids salt-tolerant crops.
europmc-pmc3022183: Brain-wave movies need mapping software. This 2011 paper brings CARTOOL, a tool that maps brain waves across time and scalp. The authors' program draws the brain's electric weather. Their software spread through labs. Epilepsy surgeons plan cuts with its maps.
europmc-pmc3033383: Gene control varies across the body's tissues. This 2011 twin study maps how gene switches differ between tissues in hundreds of women. The authors reveal tissue-specific control. Their work guides precision medicine. Fat, skin, and blood each told different stories.
europmc-pmc3047583: Brain cells got sortable barcodes. This 2011 paper finds surface flags that pick out young neurons, glia, and stem cells. The authors' markers enable pure batches. Their work aids brain repair. Pure batches make safer transplants. Mixed batches risked rogue growth.
europmc-pmc3100083: Oxidants flip cell stress switches. This 2011 review asks how oxygen radicals switch on MAPK pathways. The authors map the crosstalk. Their overview guides cell biology. The switches steer growth and death. Cancer hijacks the wiring, they show. Antioxidant drugs target the crosstalk.
europmc-pmc6510883: Doctors in Japan treat more esophageal cancer than anywhere else, and their national society turns that experience into official guidance. This is part two of the 2017 practice guidelines, laying out recommended steps for diagnosing and treating the disease. Clinicians get clear, evidence-backed instructions for each stage of care, from first tests to treatment choices.
europmc-pmc6523883: Kidney scarring - fibrosis - is the final common road of most progressive kidney disease, but testing anti-scarring drugs needs a reliable animal model. This review evaluates unilateral ureteral obstruction, where blocking one ureter in rodents triggers rapid, reproducible fibrosis. The authors weigh the model's strengths and limits for screening treatments that could slow or reverse kidney scarring.
europmc-pmc6596283: Bacteria, fungi, and plants brew a pharmacy of complex chemicals - and scientists are learning to farm the brewers instead of the brew. This review covers microbial production of natural products and biologics: engineering microbes to pump out drugs and therapies. The approach promises cheaper, greener manufacturing of tomorrow's medicines.
europmc-pmc6704583: Liver cancer exploits a subtle trick: chemical tags on RNA called m6A. This study shows the protein WTAP drives hepatocellular carcinoma by using m6A to silence a protective gene through the HuR pathway. The epigenetic hijack marks WTAP as a promising drug target.
europmc-pmc6720683: Turmeric's golden pigment - curcumin - has been folk medicine for centuries and lab obsession for decades. This wide-ranging review covers its biology, drug potential, nutraceutical uses, and how to measure it. The verdict separates genuine promise from hype for one of nature's most studied chemicals.
gao-gaoreports-b-299883: Paraclete Contracts took its 2007 award dispute to GAO, and this ruling ends it. The firm said the agency's pick violated bid law; the call measures the claims and decides. One more published verdict in the long public record of how federal contracts must be contested — and won.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-383: Ambulance bills were a lottery in 2007 — GAO's report finds costs and Medicare margins swung wildly among providers. The findings map the uneven economics of the emergency ride. The report asks what a fair price for saving lives really is, and who should set it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-483: The double-decker jumbo was coming in 2007 — GAO's report eyes the safety and capacity questions around the giant A380. The findings size up the super-jumbo's fit. The report asks whether the skies and gates were ready for the whale.
gao-gaoreports-b-299383: Able Business Technologies took its April 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest. Small tech firms get the same full hearing as the giants.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-283: Peak oil loomed over 2007, and GAO's report says the uncertainty about future supply made a strategy for the crunch essential. The findings demand the plan. The report warns that the end of cheap crude needed a playbook, not wishful thinking.
gao-gaoreports-b-299083: Fantastic Data took its February 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Great names get the same grounded hearing as all.
openalex-w7204569683: Failing kidneys show up in the mouth: gum disease, dry mouth, and sores are common in chronic kidney patients. This review gathers what dentistry knows about oral signs of kidney disease and how dentists should manage these patients. The authors map the mouth-body link for clinicians. A practical review reminding doctors that the mouth is part of the patient.
openalex-w7204270383: Menopause reshapes a woman's body and daily life. This study profiled 173 women aged 40 to 55 at two public clinics in Gurupi, Tocantins, measuring how menopause affected their quality of life. The authors map the clinical and social picture. A grounded women's-health study giving numbers to a universal transition.
openalex-w7204450783: Most people with osteoporosis learn about it only after a bone breaks. This review looks at a clever shortcut: using AI to spot the disease in CT scans taken for other reasons. The authors survey the evidence for opportunistic screening by machine. A radiology review of finding hidden illness in images already on file.
openalex-w7204165083: Who gets locked up before trial for drug trafficking, and why? This article studies the hidden risk scores judges use when ordering preventive detention. The authors argue that actuarial logic, predicting danger like an insurance table, quietly shapes decisions at the edges of rights. A critical legal study of justice by formula.
pmc-13415983: A 2026 comprehensive meta-analysis and review of intraoperative radiotherapy — radiation delivered during surgery — in colorectal cancer, examining dosage, long-term prognosis, and treatment factors. Pooling the evidence gives surgeons a clearer picture of when IORT helps. The review is a one-stop reference for the technique.
pmc-13338583: A 2026 genetics paper identifying genetic indicators of performance resilience in barrel racing quarter horses. Genomics meets rodeo: the markers could guide breeding for durable athletes. The study is a fun application of quantitative genetics.
pmc-13499683: A 2026 study on discrimination and depressive symptoms, examining how psychological resilience mediates the link across racial and ethnic groups. Resilience isn't equally protective for everyone. The findings nuance the resilience narrative with structural reality.
pmc-13524083: A 2026 plant biology paper on the red and blue light dialogue in stomatal regulation — how the two wavelengths together control the leaf pores — for water-efficient crops. Tuning light responses could save irrigation water. The study decodes the crosstalk.
pmc-13465683: This 2026 nursing study examined how practice environment and manager leadership style affect interprofessional collaboration and quality of care among acute care nurse practitioners. Leadership shapes teamwork, which shapes outcomes. The findings guide management development.
pmc-13469083: This 2026 narrative review examined the impact of resistance training on cognitive health in older adults. Lifting weights may protect the aging brain. The review gathers the evidence.
pmc-13468783: A 2026 retrospective analysis of game-based targeted nursing for children undergoing ear reconstruction for congenital microtia. Playful nursing improved the clinical experience. The study validates the approach.
pmc-13422883: In this 2026 cross-national study, cultural tightness and scientific capacity played synergistic and conflicting roles in COVID-19 outcomes. Culture and science interacted in complex ways. The study disentangles them.
pmc-13502783: This 2026 Mendelian randomization study found a causal link between polymyositis and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in European ancestry individuals. The muscle-lung connection was genetic. The causality is the finding.
pmc-13484183: A 2026 Victorian retrospective cohort study (2011–2023) on survival differences among lung cancer patients by residence location — "uneven ground." Where patients lived affected survival. The disparity is the call to action.
pmc-13481283: In this 2026 secondary analysis, moderating factors for brief psychological intervention effectiveness in probable personality disorder were examined. The intervention worked better for some. The moderators guide targeting.
pmc-13469183: This 2026 paper found distinct transposable element transcript patterns in microglia across aging and Alzheimer's disease. The jumping genes' activity marked the disease. The patterns are the discovery.
pmc-13463283: A 2026 20-year single-center cohort study of chronic kidney disease in pediatric hematopoietic stem cell transplant survivors — beyond the transplant. The survivors' kidneys were tracked. The long-term data are the value.
pmc-13594683: This 2026 paper moved from bench to bedside — clinical implications of a 4-micron surface-modulated immune response in the era of breast tissue preservation. The implant surface's immune effects were translated. The implications guide surgery.
pmc-13456983: A 2026 paper using passive sensing to isolate a biosignature for craving among individuals in early alcohol use disorder recovery. The phone sensors detected craving. The biosignature is the digital biomarker.
pmc-13454383: In this 2026 review, current advances in molecular biomarkers and liquid biopsy techniques in ovarian cancer were surveyed. The blood-based detection frontier was mapped. The review is the update.
pmc-13429283: A 2026 nationwide US survey of school nurses' perceived role responsibility, self-efficacy, and education needs in providing mental health services. The nurses' readiness was measured. The needs inform training.
pmc-13423583: A 2026 systematic review of medication non-adherence in first episode psychosis. The adherence problem was quantified. The review guides intervention.
pmc-13411283: A 2026 psychometric paper examining four mattering constructs through Rasch modeling — evidence from Turkish adolescents and college students. The mattering measures were validated. The modeling is the rigor.
pmc-13392983: This 2026 three-group study examined motivational and behavioral physical activity as differential correlates of well-being following mass trauma — direct, vicarious, and other exposure (the title is truncated). The activity-wellbeing link varied by trauma type. The correlates are the finding.
pmc-13482283: In this 2026 paper, multiomics integration uncovered metabolic control of H3K27ac in bovine inner cell masses. The embryo's epigenetics were metabolically regulated. The uncovering is the developmental insight.
pmc-13526883: This 2026 physics paper demonstrated soliton-assisted massive signal broadcasting via exceptional points. The wave physics enabled the broadcasting. The demonstrating is the advance.
pmc-13447283: A 2026 paper on molecular regulatory mechanisms of Populus deltoides under combined high temperature and short-photoperiod stress associated with DNA methylation. The cottonwood's stress epigenetics were decoded. The mechanisms are the insight.
pmc-13436083: This 2026 paper validated a checklist to evaluate emergency medicine competencies of medical students in simulation training. The assessment tool was validated. The validation serves medical education.
pmc-13614283: This 2026 paper presented an electrically switchable diffraction grating based on electrophoretic redistribution of carbon black nanoparticles. The smart grating switched on voltage. The grating is the photonic device.

arxiv-2606-16383: Bigger isn't always better. This paper presents a compact 135-million-parameter language model — tiny by modern standards — natively adapted for its target domain, arguing that efficiency can surpass raw scale. It targets practitioners who need capable AI on modest hardware, showing what careful small-model design can achieve.
arxiv-2606-16583: Visual question answering for medicine — AI answering doctors' questions about images — must be safe. This paper asks whether a model's uncertainty can serve as a safety net: not quite, but it can anticipate failures. The authors test whether uncertainty scores predict when clinical VQA models will go wrong.
